source_review.notes: Checked all six references at OWASP, Microsoft Learn, Rails Guides, or the RFC Editor. OWASP API3:2023 combines unauthorized property exposure and modification and recommends explicit property selection; the Mass Assignment Cheat Sheet recommends allowlists and DTOs. Current Microsoft model-binding documentation distinguishes form model binding from body input formatters and recommends view models for overposting protection. Current Rails Guides require explicitly permitted Strong Parameters for mass assignment. RFC 7386 confirms merge-patch null-removal/object/array behavior and server authorization responsibility; RFC 6902 confirms ordered operations and path/from semantics.

evidence: Reviewed canonical path universe P, payload p, paths(p), writable set W(c,a,x), server-owned set S, transition T_a, authorization A, invariant I, changed set Delta, and derived-effect set D_a for consistent definitions.
Confirmed all TeX commands use GitHub-compatible math delimiters and subset/disjointness relationships have correct operands.
Confirmed missing, explicit null, default, remove, DTO, command, domain object, persistence model, and response representation are distinguished.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation separates client-selected paths, authorized paths, resulting transition, and documented server-derived effects.

numerical_recomputation.notes: No quantitative benchmark, probability, entropy, cost, rate, or numerical security threshold is claimed. Example prices/counts are illustrative inputs, not computations presented as evidence.

evidence: Expanded accept into schema validity AND path subset AND transition authorization AND resulting-state invariants, confirming allowlisting alone is necessary but insufficient.
Re-derived W(c,a,x) intersection S = empty for ordinary commands, preventing direct selection of server-owned paths under complete canonical extraction.
Re-derived Delta(x,x') subset W(c,a,x) union D_a, which permits only authorized client changes and documented server-derived effects under the mapper/persistence assumptions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The subset argument is explicitly bounded by path extraction, mapper effects, persistence behavior, and policy correctness.

evidence: Reviewed unknown, duplicate, case/Unicode/alias, form/query/body precedence, wrong content type, deep/large, missing/null/empty/default, create/PUT/PATCH, and stale-version inputs.

Reviewed nested attributes, relationship connect/disconnect/set/upsert/destroy, arrays, maps/metadata, field masks, JSON Pointer escaping, JSON Patch source/destination/order/index, merge-patch arrays/null, and bulk duplicates/conflicts.

Reviewed privilege/tenant/owner/state/price/balance/version/timestamp overposting, detached ORM overwrite, bulk-hook bypass, internal/import/admin/GraphQL/gRPC paths, output exposure, old ignored fields becoming active, and model/schema drift.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review covers parsing ambiguity, direct and indirect protected properties, resulting-state violations, persistence side effects, alternate paths, and evolution regressions.

evidence: Executed strict-profile-command: the two declared profile changes were allowed; role and nested profile keys were rejected as unknown; explicit email null was accepted; stale version was denied.
Confirmed allowed profile mapping preserved server-owned role=member and tenant_id=north despite processing an update.

Checked per-operation closed schema, allowlist-over-blacklist, trusted server derivation, missing/null distinction, source-and-destination patch checks, every-element nested/bulk authorization, explicit persistence, and new-model-field-denied invariants.
invariant_checking.notes: The deterministic model demonstrates a narrow mapping boundary but intentionally omits real JSON duplicate parsing, framework binders, ORM behavior, domain authorization, and atomic persistence.

proof_review.notes: No formal noninterference, parser equivalence, authorization completeness, domain-invariant, database-isolation, or schema-evolution proof is claimed.

evidence: Confirmed the path-subset safety argument lists complete canonical extraction, no undeclared mapper effects, and exact persistence as assumptions.
Confirmed the chapter explicitly says the argument does not prove W, T_a, A, or I is correct or that every runtime path invokes it.
Confirmed framework features, DTOs, allowlists, schemas, database constraints, and tests are mechanisms or evidence layers rather than universal proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Standards semantics, bounded guarantees, implementation advice, and verification obligations are clearly separated.

evidence: Snippet report artifacts/snippets/API-047/report.json records one passing deterministic local strict-profile mapping execution with six exact outcomes.

Real decoder duplicate/alias behavior, framework binder/input formatter, ORM change tracking, database transaction, generated schema/client, mixed-version deployment, fuzzing, and penetration tests are stated as future evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live API, framework application, ORM/database, mobile fleet, or attack exercise was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed binding pipeline, separated external/domain/storage/read types, action-derived writable contracts, allowlist/default-deny evolution, unknown/duplicate semantics, server ownership, validation versus authorization/invariants, create/PUT/PATCH behavior, nested relationships, explicit persistence, independent output policy, and drift testing as one coherent command-boundary model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked deployability with closed operation DTOs, explicit mappers/commands, strict parsers and content types, presence wrappers, canonical patch paths, trusted-context derivation, authoritative relationship lookups, versioned atomic explicit-column writes, database backstops, safe errors/audit, schema diff gates, fuzz/property/mutation tests, and capability-gated mixed-version rollout. Exact framework configuration remains implementation-specific and must be tested on the active input path.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module begins with automatic binding risk, derives the closed request-to-command model, then adds ambiguity, server ownership, transition reasoning, method/patch/nesting/persistence/evolution concerns. Ten examples isolate distinct signup, blacklist drift, null, patch source, money, relationship, framework, ORM, compatibility, and GraphQL cases; five exercises progress to infrastructure provisioning transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
